newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nintendo says earnings in line with forecast.
newsitem.headline: Nintendo says earnings in line with forecast.

text.p: Nintendo Co Ltd said on Tuesday that its earnings so far this business year were generally in line with its forecast due to robust sales of its 64-bit game machine and software in overseas markets.

"Sales of software launched in July in the United States have been very good. Our U.S. unit is also confident of hitting its sales target for hardware," Nintendo managing director Hiroshi Imanishi told Reuters.
Earlier this month, Nintendo of America said retailers had sold a record 300,000 copies of its Star Fox 64 video game within five days of its launch.
The Nintendo 64 console is also selling well in Europe and sales of software for it are increasing, Imanishi said.
But in Japan the console has been selling at the same pace this business year as last business year.
"Sales of Nintendo 64 in Japan are so-so. Compared with Sony's PlayStation, our sales have been low as we missed two Christmas shopping seasons due to development delays," Imanishi said.
Nintendo 64 was launched in 1996. The 64-bit system allows users to play more sophisticated and complicated games than older generation systems like Nintendo's pervious 16-bit system.
Sony's rival PlayStation is a 32-bit machine.
Imanishi said Nintendo does not plan to reduce Nintendo 64 prices in Japan to boost sales.
"We believe sales will jump if we have some hit software before Christmas," he said.

He said the number of software titles for the Nintendo 64 was limited at the moment, but added that Nintendo felt that maintaining the high quality of the software was the best way to promote video games.
In the current business year to March 31, Nintendo expects to sell three million Nintendo 64 machines in Japan and six million in North America.
It sold 2.04 million units in Japan from last June until this March, and 3.42 million in North America from last September until this March.

Imanishi said Nintendo's earnings for 1997/98 were mostly in line with its May forecast which projected group net profit of 67 billion yen ($567 million) against actual group net profit of 65.48 billion yen ($554 million) in 1996/97.
It said group sales in 1997/98 would grow to 490 billion yen ($4.15 billion), up from 418.21 billion yen ($3.54 billion) in 1996/97.
The forecasts were made based on an exchange rate of 120 yen to the dollar, Imanishi said. On Tuesday, the dollar was traded around 117.70 yen.
"If the exchange rate stays at the current level, there may be some impact on our earnings but we are trying to reduce any such impact," Imanishi said without elaborating.
Imanishi said Nintendo may introduce a stock option scheme for its employees and added that the company was still looking at the tax implications of doing so. ($1=118)
